summary: Sporting News previews the Manchester United vs Chelsea Premier League match at Old Trafford in December 2023 by reviewing their all-time head-to-head record. United lead the historical results and are unbeaten in 11 league games against Chelsea since November 2017, though the fixture is the most drawn in Premier League history. The article also traces the rivalry's peak after Roman Abramovich's 2004 takeover and compares each club's trophy hauls.
one_line: Overview of the Manchester United vs Chelsea all-time head-to-head record, recent results and the history of their rivalry ahead of a December 2023 Old Trafford match.
key_facts: Across all competitions Manchester United and Chelsea have played 193 games: United 82 wins, Chelsea 55 wins, 56 draws.
Manchester United beat Chelsea 4-1 at Old Trafford on May 25, 2023, the most recent meeting before the December 2023 game.
Manchester United are 11 Premier League games unbeaten against Chelsea since November 2017, and seven of those ended in draws.
The fixture is the most drawn in Premier League history; a 1-1 draw is the most common exact Premier League scoreline, occurring 14 times.
In the 2008 UEFA Champions League final, Edwin van der Sar saved Nicholas Anelka's penalty to give United victory after a 1-1 draw after extra time.
The teams have met in three FA Cup finals; Eden Hazard's penalty gave Chelsea a 1-0 win in 2018, and Hazard also scored the only goal when Chelsea beat United in 2007 after extra time.
United beat Chelsea 4-0 in the 1994 FA Cup final under Sir Alex Ferguson.
After Roman Abramovich took over Chelsea in 2004, United lost five and won one of the next nine games between the teams.
In 2004/05 Chelsea won the title 18 points ahead of third-placed United, who had to give them a guard of honour at Old Trafford.
United have a record 20 Premier League titles and Chelsea six; United have 12 FA Cup wins, eight more than Chelsea.
Chelsea have won the Champions League and Europa League twice each, while United have won the former three times and the latter once.
In 2022/23 United finished third while Chelsea came 12th, their lowest final position for 29 years.
